text:
alex: Heads-up: I reproduced a high P99 in CI for long-context requests when continuous batching is enabled. Looks like KV cache paging + batch merge are interacting badly and causing head-of-line blocking.

mira: Can you share repro steps and profiler output? :eyes:

alex: Repro summary: run load test with mix of 1-token and 64k-context requests (heavy-tail arrival). Continuous batcher merged a tiny request into a big 64k request. The merged batch triggers interleaved KV accesses that evict head pages while the big request repopulates the cache. Quick log excerpt below.

alex: ```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] batch_merge id=abc len=2 sizes=(1,65536)
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] kvcache:get key=mdl-xyz idx=456 -> page_fault wait=12ms
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] evict_page idx=123 reason=mem_pressure slab=kvcache free=8MB
[2026-03-15T10:12:04Z] p99_latency_ms=432
```

sam: That looks like classic head-of-line blocking. Small request ends up queued behind big cache refill. Did you check page fetch concurrency or fragment lock contention?

alex: Yep. Perf + pprof show hot stalls on page_fault_wait and page_fetch_io. Heap snapshots show steady memory growth during a long session (64k sequences) due to fragmented free ranges. Here's the flame link: https://internal/fg/1781 (pprof attached in ticket).

mira: Kernel selection might be amplifying this. Large-seq kernels pick different memory tiling and can spike temporary buffers during KV repopulation. If the merged batch triggers the large kernel, the memory pressure can force paging earlier. Try forcing the small-seq kernel when a small request is merged into a large one as a quick mitigation.

liam: Quick experiment: added a heuristic that avoids merging tiny requests into any batch that contains an active large-context request (threshold: >32k tokens). Split instead. Staging numbers: P99 dropped from ~430ms -> ~85ms. CPU/GPU utilization unchanged. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy-bot: rolled patch kvcache-batch-split-heuristic -> staging (build 9082).

alex: Also observed fragmentation pattern: evicted pages leave behind many small free intervals, so subsequent allocations go to slow-path and trigger more paging. A compaction/pin for head pages for active sessions might help.

sam: Could we implement session-aware pinning (pin first N pages of a recently active session) plus an LRU that biases by session recency? Might reduce page_fault_rate per session.

mira: I'll add dashboards: per-batch merged_large_count, page_fault_rate, page_eviction_count, and average contiguous-free-run-length. That should make regressions visible.

alex: Filed PERF-2389 with traces, repro script, pprof outputs, and suggested mitigations (split heuristic, small-kernel override, head-page pinning). Assigning @sam and @mira to triage.

liam: For follow-up: we should also audit the continuous-batcher config: merging policy currently only considers latency/cost, not KV locality. Add a locality score so merging prefers requests that share prefix/context.

alex: Agreed. Thanks everyone. Will drop the repro + a short runbook in the ticket.

mira: Nice find. Let's keep it minimal in prod: enable split heuristic behind a flag and monitor the new metrics.

alex: Done. FLAG: kvcache.split_on_large_merge=true staged.

sam: I'll start the triage tomorrow and attempt a pinning PoC.

alex: TY. :rocket:
